item.title: Tinubu Hails Bakassi Seaport, Says Project Will Create Jobs, Boost Trade
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has described the groundbreaking of the Bakassi Deep Seaport in Cross River State as a major milestone in Nigeria’s economic diversification, saying the project will open new commercial corridors, stimulate industrialisation and create jobs. Represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima at the ceremony in Bakassi on Friday, November 13, 2026, Tinubu commended Governor Bassey Otu and the people of Cross River for sustaining the project’s vision and moving it towards actualisation. The President recalled that the project was conceived in 2014, with an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment developed in March 2015, before receiving fresh impetus under Otu. Designed with a 20-metre draft, the port is expected to accommodate large vessels that currently bypass Nigerian ports. It is also linked to a 260-kilometre superhighway intended to facilitate the movement of cargo to markets across the country. Tinubu credited Otu’s determination with helping to overcome institutional and financial challenges, including efforts to secure a $3.5 billion financing arrangement with Afreximbank and formalise the Public-Private Partnership framework in February 2025. “This is beyond a Cross River dream. It is a Nigerian project. It is a poverty breaker,” he said. President Kashim Shettima at the ceremony in Bakassi on Friday Tinubu stressed that the Bakassi port would complement, rather than compete with, Lagos, which handles more than 80 per cent of Nigeria’s foreign trade. “Lagos is not our enemy. Lagos is our elder brother in trade. No country eats with one hand. No country carries all its loads on one shoulder. That shoulder will break,” he said. He argued that establishing another major maritime gateway would reduce pressure on Lagos ports, ease congestion and lower costs. “When Calabar works, Nigeria works on two legs,” the President added. He said Nigeria had not fully exploited its coastline along the Gulf of Guinea, while neighbouring countries continued to benefit from trade that could be attracted to Nigerian ports. Tinubu said the Bakassi project would help retain regional cargo, expand access to international markets and strengthen Nigeria’s competitiveness in maritime trade. He noted that about 90 per cent of cargo moves by sea, but Nigeria handles only a fraction of regional cargo trade despite its economic position in West Africa. The port, he said, would help close the gap, reduce dependence on a single maritime gateway and enable the country to capture a larger share of regional commerce. Shettima and Governor Otu at the groundbreaking event. The President also acknowledged the territorial and economic losses suffered by Cross River following the Bakassi Peninsula ruling and the loss of oil revenue. item.title: Lagos NDC meeting attack threatens democracy — APM candidate
item.description: By Dapo Akinrefon The governorship candidate of the Action Peoples Movement (APM) in Lagos State, Prince Laja Adeoye, has condemned the attack on supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during their town hall meeting in Lagos, describing the incident as shameful and a threat to democracy. Adeoye said the disruption of the meeting at Classique Event Centre, Oregun, Ikeja, on Thursday, amounted to an infringement on the constitutional rights of citizens to assemble and freely express their political views. He warned that the use of thugs to disrupt opposition gatherings could heighten political tension ahead of the 2027 general elections. Adeoye said, “Nobody should be attacked for supporting a candidate of his or her choice. What happened in Lagos on Thursday was shameful and unacceptable in a democracy.” He described the incident as particularly disturbing, noting that Lagos had traditionally been regarded as a centre of political activities where parties and candidates could canvass for support. According to him, the attack was not merely against the NDC but also against the democratic process and Nigerians who believe in free and fair elections. The APM candidate urged the Lagos State Police Command to identify, arrest and prosecute those responsible for the incident, irrespective of their political affiliation or status. He warned that failure to bring the perpetrators to justice could encourage similar attacks in other parts of the country as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 elections. Adeoye also expressed concern over the safety of voters, candidates and journalists during the campaign period, recalling reports that a journalist covering the meeting was attacked and dispossessed of his working equipment. He called on political leaders to rise above partisan interests and condemn violence, stressing that democracy could not thrive in an atmosphere of fear and intimidation. The APM candidate commended the NDC supporters for maintaining their composure despite the alleged provocation, saying their conduct demonstrated commitment to democratic values. “The supporters did not retaliate. They conducted themselves in a peaceful manner. That is the spirit we need to sustain our democracy,” he said. He urged political parties to caution their supporters against violence and embrace issue-based campaigns rather than intimidation and thuggery. Adeoye also called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), security agencies and other political stakeholders to work together to guarantee a level playing field for all parties ahead of the 2027 elections. He said Lagos, as the country’s commercial nerve centre, should demonstrate that elections could be contested and won without violence. He further urged the National Peace Committee and civil society organisations to intervene by encouraging political actors to embrace peaceful political engagement. item.title: Nasarawa pensioners begin enforcement of ₦4bn court order
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia A group of 601 retired civil servants in Nasarawa State has commenced enforcement of a court order directing the recovery of over ₦4 billion in outstanding gratuities and other entitlements owed them by the state government. The pensioners, under the aegis of the Concerned Group of Nasarawa State Pensioners, secured a consent judgment against the state government in 2020 over the alleged non-payment of their retirement benefits. Their spokespersons, Mr Simon Auna and Mallam Usman Adamu, disclosed the development while speaking with journalists in Lafia on Friday. The group said it subsequently obtained an order from the National Industrial Court, Makurdi, awarding 25 per cent post-judgment interest on the judgment sum, bringing the total amount being sought to over ₦4 billion. According to the pensioners, following the alleged failure of the state government to comply with the judgment, their lawyers approached the Senior District Court in Makurdi, presided over by Justice Ada Jack. The court subsequently directed six commercial banks to release funds belonging to the Nasarawa State Government, amounting to over ₦4 billion, for payment to the affected retirees. In a move to enforce the order, the pensioners’ legal team, accompanied by court bailiffs, visited some branches of one of the commercial banks in Makurdi, Benue State, where they removed some movable properties. Speaking on the development, counsel to the pensioners, Mrs Doofan Sefa-Aii, said the legal team would continue to operate within the law to ensure full recovery of the funds owed the retirees. Another counsel, Mr Awo Matthew, appealed to the Nasarawa State Government and the banks involved to allow the legal process to take its course, considering the hardship the pensioners had endured while pursuing payment of their entitlements. However, the Director of Corporate Services and Arbitration at the Nasarawa State Ministry of Justice, Mr Usman Aliyu, said the state government had taken all necessary legal steps, including filing a motion for a stay of execution of the court order. Meanwhile, Adamu, who is the group’s Lafia Local Government Chairman, and Auna, its Legal Adviser, described the court order as a significant breakthrough after years of seeking payment of their entitlements. They said the development had renewed their hope of recovering the outstanding benefits. The pensioners reaffirmed their determination to pursue their entitlements through lawful means until the matter was resolved. item.title: Zulum offers soldiers N50,000 each, logistics for Borno deployment
item.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri Borno State Governor, Professor Babagana Umara Zulum, has announced a ₦50,000 welfare support for each soldier preparing for deployment to Maiwa and Koshebe communities in the state, alongside a pledge to provide operational logistics to strengthen security. Zulum gave the assurance on Friday during a visit to the headquarters of the 24 Task Force Brigade in Dikwa Local Government Area, where he met with the Brigade Commander, Brigadier General Aminu Gumel. The governor said the visit was aimed at exploring measures to improve security along the Maiduguri–Mafa–Dikwa–Ngala highway, a strategic economic corridor linking several communities in eastern Borno State. He noted that the highway was vital to trade, transportation and cross-border commercial activities, stressing that improved security would enable residents to travel safely, move agricultural produce and rebuild their livelihoods. “My visit is primarily aimed at exploring measures to strengthen security along the strategic economic corridor, which connects Maiduguri to several communities in eastern Borno and serves as a vital route for trade, transportation and cross-border commercial activities,” Zulum said. Addressing troops preparing for deployment to Maiwa and Koshebe, the governor pledged to provide operational logistics and sustained welfare support. He also announced a payment of ₦50,000 to each soldier preparing for the deployment to the two communities. Koshebe has previously suffered deadly attacks by suspected Boko Haram insurgents. On November 28, 2020, insurgents attacked rice farmers working in fields around the community, killing more than 100 people, many of whom were seasonal farm labourers from Sokoto State. Similarly, in November 2023, suspected insurgents attacked farmers harvesting rice in the Karkut and Koshebe areas of Mafa Local Government Area, killing at least 13 people, while others were reported missing. Zulum’s administration has continued to provide logistics and welfare assistance to security agencies as part of efforts to support military operations, improve security and facilitate the return of displaced residents to their communities. The governor was accompanied on the visit by the member representing Monguno/Nganzai/Marte Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Engr. Bukar Talba; member representing Dikwa Constituency in the Borno State House of Assembly, Mohammed Zakariya; Commissioner for Information and Internal Security, Professor Usman Tar; Commissioner for Local Government and Emirate Affairs, Sugun Mai Mele; and other senior government officials. item.title: COVID-19 loans must be repaid, NIRSAL MFB insists
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief NIRSAL Microfinance Bank (NMFB) has clarified that the COVID-19 Targeted Credit Facility (TCF) was an intervention loan, not a grant, stressing that beneficiaries are obligated to repay the funds. The bank said deductions from the accounts of beneficiaries who accessed the facility would continue until their outstanding loans were fully liquidated, in line with the Global Standing Instruction (GSI) mechanism. In a statement issued in Abuja at the weekend, the bank explained that the GSI framework allows financial institutions to recover outstanding loan obligations from eligible accounts linked to borrowers’ Bank Verification Numbers (BVNs), subject to applicable regulatory guidelines. The bank said the clarification became necessary to address concerns surrounding loan recoveries and reassure customers and members of the public of its commitment to transparency, accountability and responsible banking practices. It explained that the COVID-19 Targeted Credit Facility was introduced by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to support households and businesses affected by the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. According to the bank, all beneficiaries were required to accept electronic offer letters before disbursement, with the documents clearly outlining the terms and conditions of the facility, including repayment obligations and recovery mechanisms in cases of default. “Regarding the recovery process, the Bank operates within the applicable regulatory framework, including the Global Standing Instruction (GSI) mechanism approved by the Central Bank of Nigeria,” it stated. NIRSAL MFB, however, acknowledged concerns raised by some beneficiaries over the timing and amounts of deductions, outstanding loan balances and access to repayment information. The bank said it took the complaints seriously, noting that customers must have access to accurate information about their loan accounts. It stressed that the deductions were intended to settle outstanding contractual obligations, adding that beneficiaries who disputed deductions or identified discrepancies in their repayment records should contact the bank for individual account reconciliation. “Where any beneficiary has concerns about deductions made, discrepancies in repayment records or the status of an outstanding balance, such cases should be brought to the bank’s attention for individual account reconciliation and appropriate resolution,” it said. The bank assured that legitimate complaints would be investigated and that any discrepancies established during the reconciliation process would receive the necessary attention. It urged beneficiaries seeking clarification on their loan status, repayment history or outstanding obligations to contact the bank through its officially designated customer service channels. item.title: Customs intercepts live sea turtle at Nigeria-Benin border
item.description: By Efe Onodjae The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Seme Area Command, has intercepted a live endangered sea turtle allegedly being smuggled through a footpath linking Nigeria and the Republic of Benin. The Olive Ridley Sea Turtle, scientifically known as Lepidochelys olivacea, was intercepted during a routine patrol by Customs officers at about 10.30pm on Thursday, November 12, 2026. The command said the officers sighted a suspicious individual carrying a sack along the border route, but the suspect abandoned the bag and fled into a nearby bush upon noticing the patrol team. According to a statement by the command’s Public Relations Officer, Superintendent of Customs, John Tunde Ayagbalo, examination of the abandoned sack revealed the live sea turtle concealed inside. He said the animal was immediately secured and kept in safe custody before being handed over to relevant wildlife authorities for proper care, rehabilitation and eventual release into its natural habitat. The Acting Customs Area Controller, Seme Area Command, Deputy Comptroller Norman Olisah Alumanah, described the interception as a demonstration of the vigilance and professionalism of officers in tackling wildlife trafficking. Alumanah warned smugglers, poachers and their collaborators against using the nation’s borders as corridors for illegal wildlife trade, adding that the command had intensified patrols, surveillance and intelligence gathering across its area of responsibility. He also called on residents of border communities to provide credible intelligence to support the fight against wildlife trafficking. The Customs boss said the command would complement enforcement operations with stakeholder education and sensitisation on endangered species, their ecological importance and the legal implications of their unauthorised trade. Wildlife trafficking remains a major environmental crime, threatening biodiversity and the survival of endangered species through illegal exploitation for meat, eggs, shells, traditional medicine and the exotic pet trade. Nigeria is a signatory to the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), which regulates international trade in endangered wildlife and plant species. The convention is domesticated in Nigeria through the Endangered Species (Control of International Trade and Traffic) Act, Cap E9, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004. item.title: Ebola: All 62 contacts test negative after monitoring – NCDC
item.description: By Chidinma Chukwu ABUJA — The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has completed the 21-day monitoring of all 62 contacts linked to the imported case of Bundibugyo Virus Disease (BVD), a form of Ebola disease, confirmed in the Federal Capital Territory on October 20, 2026, with no secondary infections recorded. The Director-General of NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, disclosed this on Friday during a media briefing in Abuja, saying the last contact had been discharged from monitoring after testing negative for the virus. Idris said 13 of the 62 contacts reported fever or other non-specific symptoms during the monitoring period, but laboratory tests confirmed that none had contracted the disease. “The 21-day monitoring period for contacts linked to the index case has been completed, with the last contact discharged today. We are glad to announce that none of the contacts became ill with the disease, meaning no transmission from the index case. “A total of 62 contacts were identified, placed in quarantine and followed up by our public health teams. During the monitoring period, 13 contacts reported fever or other non-specific symptoms. All 13 were tested for Bundibugyo Virus Disease, and all tested negative,” he said. The index case was a 42-year-old Ugandan-born woman, who tested positive for the virus in Abuja on October 20. She was subsequently medically evacuated to Switzerland on October 26. Providing an update on her condition, Idris said the woman had recovered and been discharged from a hospital in Geneva. He also disclosed that seven additional suspected cases were reported and investigated in Adamawa, Rivers, Borno, Lagos and Ekiti states within the past three weeks. All seven cases tested negative for the virus. However, the NCDC chief cautioned against interpreting the completion of contact monitoring as a formal declaration that the outbreak was over. He explained that such a declaration would depend on established public health criteria and findings from continued surveillance. “It is important to note that the completion of contact monitoring does not, by itself, constitute a formal declaration that an outbreak is over. Such a determination must be based on the applicable public health criteria and the findings of ongoing surveillance. “Nigeria therefore remains vigilant, particularly given the continued occurrence of Ebola virus disease in the DRC,” he said. Idris assured Nigerians that disease surveillance and preparedness activities would continue, stressing that the agency remained committed to protecting residents and visitors. Looking ahead to the December festive season, he warned that increased travel, social interactions and large public gatherings could heighten the risk of disease transmission. He identified family celebrations, religious activities, political campaigns, concerts, festivals and sporting events as occasions likely to increase human movement and interaction. item.title: 2027: Tinubu, Atiku, Obi not there for Nigeria — Sule Lamido
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Jigawa State Governor and PDP chieftain, Sule Lamido, has dismissed President Bola Tinubu, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and former Anambra State Governor, Peter Obi, as unsuitable options for Nigeria ahead of the 2027 general election. Lamido stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, where he was asked which of the three political figures could attract the Northern vote in the forthcoming presidential election. Giving his assessment, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) chieftain said none of the three contenders was in a position to address Nigeria’s challenges. He said, “Look, from my own personal opinion, in my view, voting should depend on who is the person with the right kind of quality and calibre to be able to address the same problem. Peter Obi, Tinubu, Atiku — none of them is there for Nigeria.” The former Jigawa governor also declared his support for the PDP’s presidential candidate, Professor Sandy Onor, insisting that he remained committed to the opposition party and would not vote for Tinubu in 2027. Asked whether he had endorsed Tinubu for a second term, Lamido said he remained a PDP member and would vote for his party’s candidate. He said, “I am PDP through and through. I am voting for my candidate, Professor Sandy Onor; that is my candidate. What I’m saying is that we have somebody called Professor Onor on that ballot. I’m voting him.” Lamido’s remarks come amid controversy over claims that he had endorsed Tinubu’s re-election bid after Vice-President Kashim Shettima reportedly listed him among former Jigawa governors backing the President ahead of 2027. However, the Jigawa State chapter of the PDP had earlier dismissed the claim, insisting that Lamido had neither endorsed Tinubu nor defected to the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC. item.title: NSCDC disbands anti-vandalism outpost after Gombe incident
item.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Gombe State Command, has ordered the immediate disbandment of its Anti-Vandalism Outpost following an incident involving its personnel and a truck driver in the state. The incident, which occurred on Thursday, November 12, 2026, reportedly followed a misunderstanding between personnel of the unit and a truck driver, resulting in the discharge of a firearm. The State Commandant, Commandant Muhammed Inuwa Usman, mni, also summoned all Officers-in-Charge (OCs) of the various formations and outposts to an emergency meeting on Friday to address the incident and reinforce professional standards among personnel. In a statement issued on Friday, the Command’s Public Relations Officer, Chief Superintendent of Corps Buhari Sa’ad, said the meeting was convened to address the incident and strengthen discipline and accountability within the command. During the meeting, Usman cautioned the officers against unprofessional conduct, indiscipline and actions capable of undermining the image of the Corps. He emphasised the need for personnel to remain professional, disciplined and civil, while respecting the fundamental human rights of members of the public in the discharge of their statutory responsibilities. The commandant also stressed that the use of firearms must strictly comply with established rules, operational procedures and applicable regulations, warning officers against taking the law into their own hands. As part of the disciplinary and administrative measures, he ordered the immediate disbandment of the Anti-Vandalism Outpost and directed all personnel attached to the unit to report to the State Command Headquarters without delay. Usman reiterated that the Corps would not condone indiscipline, abuse of authority or violations of citizens’ rights. He urged outpost commanders to strengthen supervision of their personnel and ensure strict adherence to the highest standards of professionalism and accountability. The commandant assured residents that the NSCDC remained committed to protecting lives and property, respecting human rights and maintaining peace and order in Gombe State. item.title: England boss Tuchel eager to end Spain’s unbeaten run
item.description: Thomas Tuchel believes England are ready to end Spain’s unbeaten record when they face the world and European champions in Madrid on Sunday. While victory offers not much more than the prospect of a more favourable Nations League quarter-final in March, it would be a landmark moment for England if they could end Spain’s run of 43 matches without defeat. “It (Spain) is a team that has forgotten how to lose, so of course it requires a top performance first of all, and if we can deliver this performance, it will give us a big boost,” said England manager Tuchel, whose side beat Croatia 2-1 at Wembley on Thursday. “I think we’re there, and I think we’re ready to win on Sunday,” the German added. “I know what it takes, and no one can ever guarantee it, but I think it’s the moment to check how far we are and to push our limit and proof of concept.” England lost the reverse fixture 3-2 at Wembley in September, but it might have been a different story had Harry Kane scored a penalty to put Tuchel’s team 3-1 up. “It’s important that we play with the same mindset that we played at home, and attack them and try to make it a physical game, and try to impose our strength.” England players have previously faced racist abuse in Spain, with Ashley Cole and Shaun Wright-Phillips targeted during a friendly in Madrid in 2004. Spain, meanwhile, must play their next home friendly with a reduced capacity as a punishment for supporters singing a discriminatory chant about Muslims during a fixture against Egypt in March. “We will never accept racism,” said Tuchel. “We will never be racist towards anyone.” He added: “I expect, of course, full support from the Spanish crowd for the Spanish team. But we will not expect anything. And I think the referee and the officials know about that… There is a protocol in place and it’s important that the players know about the protocol. “We will give our answers if stuff like this happens. Best answers are on the pitch.” The post England boss Tuchel eager to end Spain’s unbeaten run appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: APC Italy disowns planned Torino event
item.description: By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA — The All Progressives Congress (APC), Italy Chapter, has dissociated itself from a purported party event scheduled to hold in Torino, Italy, on November 28, 2026, saying the gathering was not authorised by its leadership. The chapter urged party members and supporters in Italy and the diaspora to disregard the invitation, which advertised Hotel Royal Torino as the venue. The position was contained in a statement signed by the APC Italy Chairman and member of the APC-Diaspora Directorate of the Presidential Campaign Council, Amb. Prince Chima Ibezim. Ibezim said the party leadership in Italy and Nigeria had neither approved the event nor been formally informed of its organisation. “The attention of the APC Italy has been brought to a purported event in the name of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Italy Chapter, scheduled to hold in Torino on November 28, 2026, at Hotel Royal Torino. “The leadership of the party in Italy and Nigeria has not approved the event and is not aware of its organisation,” he said. Ibezim stated that the chapter had contacted Hotel Royal regarding the proposed gathering and was informed that no booking had been made for the event on the advertised date. He advised party members and supporters to avoid attending any gathering not officially communicated or endorsed by the recognised chapter leadership. The chairman said all official APC Italy programmes, activities and enquiries would be communicated through the chapter’s recognised leadership structure and authorised representatives. He urged members to rely on official party channels for information about its activities and engagements. The post APC Italy disowns planned Torino event appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigeria, EU seal €20m defence support deal
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — Nigeria and the European Union have concluded arrangements for a €20 million defence support package aimed at strengthening the operational capabilities of the Armed Forces, particularly in counterterrorism operations in the Lake Chad Basin. The agreement, the EU’s first bilateral defence support package to Nigeria, is being provided under the European Peace Facility (EPF). The Minister of Defence, Gen. Christopher Gwabin Musa (retd.), disclosed this during a meeting with a delegation from the European External Action Service (EEAS), led by the Head of the European Peace Facility, Claire Gaudin, at the Ministry of Defence Headquarters, Ship House, Abuja. According to a statement issued by the Special Assistant (Media) to the minister, Leah Katung-Babatunde, the meeting focused on finalising arrangements for the delivery of the support package, which was sealed in October 2026. Speaking during the meeting, Musa reaffirmed Nigeria’s commitment to developing indigenous defence capabilities and achieving self-sufficiency in military equipment and technology. He welcomed the EU assistance, describing it as a boost to the operational effectiveness of Nigerian troops engaged in security operations. The minister urged the EU to build on the momentum generated by the recently concluded Africa Defence Exhibition (AFRIDEX) by supporting the establishment of local defence production lines in Nigeria. He also reiterated Nigeria’s determination to track and dismantle terrorist financing networks across the world, irrespective of where they operate. Musa explained that the current phase of the EU support would focus on non-lethal military supplies, including equipment, technical training and maintenance. He expressed optimism that subsequent phases would cover other critical areas, particularly military medical support and advanced surveillance capabilities. Earlier, Gaudin said the €20 million package would provide counter-improvised explosive device (C-IED) equipment, counter-unmanned aircraft systems (C-UAS), night-vision capabilities and personal protective equipment for troops deployed in operational theatres. She said the priority areas were jointly identified and agreed upon with the leadership of the Armed Forces of Nigeria following extensive bilateral consultations. Gaudin added that Nigeria was among more than 20 African countries and 30 beneficiaries globally receiving assistance under the European Peace Facility. She said the package would complement wider regional stabilisation efforts, particularly operations under the Multinational Joint Task Force (MNJTF). The Nigerian and EU delegations also explored opportunities to deepen security cooperation in maritime operations, with particular attention to strengthening security across the Gulf of Guinea. item.title: Pochettino sheds tears, explains why he left USA for Man Utd
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Mauricio Pochettino broke down in tears as he explained his decision to accept Manchester United’s offer after only recently signing a new contract with the United States national team. The Argentine described leaving the USA job as “one of the most difficult” decisions of his career. According to BBC Sport, Pochettino was announced as Michael Carrick’s successor on Friday and has signed a two-and-a-half-year deal at Old Trafford. United triggered a release clause of about £7.4 million, with a further payment for his backroom staff. “It’s difficult to talk now,” Pochettino said at his first news conference after the move was confirmed. “I’m a very emotional guy. It’s a very sad decision.” The 54-year-old said the chance to manage Manchester United was too rare to turn down. “I never said I wanted to go back, but they know there aren’t too many opportunities that happen in your career like Manchester United,” he said. “When it arrives, it’s difficult to turn down.” Pochettino signed a new four-year contract with the USA in the summer but will lead the national team in matches against Haiti on November 14 and 18 before departing for Manchester. Carrick was sacked on Thursday after United’s worst start to a domestic campaign in 40 years. The club are 18th in the Premier League after winning once in 10 league matches and sit one point above bottom-placed Sunderland. Pochettino’s first match in charge is scheduled to be away to Liverpool on November 22. The post Pochettino sheds tears, explains why he left USA for Man Utd appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ondo APC denies rift, declares unity ahead of 2027
item.description: …Says no member is left out of reconciliation efforts By Dayo Johnson, Akure The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Ondo State has dismissed reports of rivalry and divisions among its leaders, declaring that the party is united and ready for the 2027 general elections. The state chairman, Hon. Babatunde Kolawole, expressed confidence that the party would secure victories for President Bola Tinubu and its other candidates, insisting that ongoing reconciliation efforts were yielding positive results. Speaking with journalists in Akure, Kolawole said no member or interest group had been excluded from efforts to strengthen the party and bring all tendencies together. He said there was no reason for members to regard one another as rivals, particularly as Ondo State would not hold a governorship election in 2027 and Tinubu had emerged as the party’s sole presidential candidate. “Therefore, there is no rivalry. There is no cause for alarm. I can assure you we are on top of it and everything will be okay,” he said. Kolawole thanked Tinubu and the APC National Chairman for their support, while commending Senate Leader, Senator Michael Opeyemi Bamidele, and other party members for their contributions to the success of the presidential campaign. Also speaking, the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign in Ondo State, Rt. Hon. Victor Olabimtan, reaffirmed the party’s unity, disclosing that the reconciliation committee established after the party congress had reached out to various party organs, interest groups and individuals. He said the committee had extended its engagements beyond the state, including visits to Abuja and Lagos, as part of efforts to bring aggrieved members back into the party’s fold. Olabimtan cited the participation of previously estranged leaders, including Wale Akinterinwa and Princess Oladunni Odu, at the recent presidential campaign rally in Ondo State as evidence that the reconciliation process was making progress. He said he had personally reached out to some party leaders, adding that Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa had also made the unification of different tendencies a priority since emerging as the party’s leader in the state. According to him, Tinubu’s emergence as the APC’s presidential candidate offered members an opportunity to put their differences aside and consolidate the party’s unity. “Nobody is left out. All we need to do is to ensure that we put more effort into strengthening the existing unity that we are all enjoying in the party today. “So, there is no cause for alarm. As we make progress, you will also see that our efforts, the efforts of the governor, the party and its leaders are indeed yielding fruits to ensure that everybody is brought on board,” he said. Olabimtan expressed confidence that the reconciliation efforts would translate into electoral victories for Tinubu, as well as the party’s candidates for the Senate, House of Representatives and state and national assemblies. item.title: 2027: Whoever Wins Nigeria Loses, Atiku, Obi Handing Tinubu Advantage – Sule Lamido
item.description: Former Jigawa State Governor Sule Lamido has criticised opposition figures Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi for failing to unite ahead of the 2027 presidential election, saying their division gives President Bola Tinubu an advantage. Lamido, who is a chieftain of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), said a united opposition would have posed a stronger challenge to Tinubu, suggesting that Atiku could have emerged as the presidential candidate, with Obi as his running mate. He spoke on Friday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today, where he was asked whether the 2027 election could produce a similar outcome to the 2023 contest, in which Tinubu defeated Atiku and Obi. “I think the way things are, the propaganda and support warfare is too much. It’s too intense for even Nigeria to be able to really understand what’s happening,” he said. Former Jigawa governor of Jigawa State, Sule Lamido Lamido attributed the opposition’s difficulties partly to the number of serving and former governors in the All Progressives Congress (APC), as well as the failure of Atiku and Obi to work together. “Because of the number of governors, both serving and former governors of the APC, and because Atiku and Obi divided their own force, it gives Tinubu the advantage,” he said. FILE: Peter Obi (L) and Atiku Abubakar (R) The former governor argued that the two opposition leaders were effectively strengthening Tinubu’s chances by pursuing separate political ambitions. “So both Peter Obi and Atiku are simply handing Tinubu, very easily. But if they come together, it would have been a high-level canvas, you know, Atiku for president and Obi running mate, and then after four years, one takes over,” he said. Whoever Wins? Two years after the 2023 presidential election, Obi and Atiku left the Labour Party (LP) and PDP, respectively, to pursue a united opposition front ahead of the 2027 elections. In July 2025, opposition leaders adopted the African Democratic Congress (ADC) as a common platform to challenge President Bola Tinubu. However, internal disagreements over party leadership, structure and presidential ambitions weakened the coalition. Kwankwaso and Obi defected to the NDC from the ADC. X/@KwankwasoRM The crisis eventually saw Obi leave the ADC alongside Rabiu Kwankwaso for the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in May 2026, where Obi was subsequently adopted as its 2027 presidential candidate. Atiku, on the other hand, remained in the ADC and won its presidential primary. Atiku (centre) is the presidential candidate of the ADC for the 2027 general elections. Despite their separate political platforms, both opposition leaders have continued their pursuit ahead of the 2027 election. Obi has maintained that any alliance with Atiku must be based on a formal agreement between their parties, rather than a personal arrangement. item.title: 2027: APC benefits from Atiku, Obi presidential ambitions – Keyamo
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has disclosed that the All Progressives Congress (APC) would prefer former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and former Anambra State Governor, Peter Obi, to participate in the 2027 presidential election to prevent opposition parties from uniting under a single political platform. Keyamo said having both opposition figures on the ballot would serve the ruling party’s political interest by preventing opposition supporters from consolidating their strength behind one candidate. Speaking on Friday during an interview on Frontline, a current affairs programme on Eagle 102.5 FM, Ilese-Ijebu, the minister made the clarification while responding to questions about his earlier comment that heaven would not fall if Atiku Abubakar was absent from the 2027 presidential ballot following the leadership crisis in the African Democratic Congress (ADC). He said, “It is in our interest that Atiku Abubakar and Obi run so that all opposition will not gather under one umbrella.” Keyamo, however, dismissed allegations that the Federal Government or the APC was using state institutions to frustrate opposition parties, insisting that the judiciary was responding to complaints by members of the ADC who felt deprived of their rights during the party’s leadership crisis. He argued that the controversy was being presented as an attempt to prevent a major opposition figure from contesting, while the grievances of other party members who claimed to have been displaced were being overlooked. The minister said, “The judiciary is acting on genuine complaints of Nigerians who are pained. Nigerians who are deprived of their rights in ADC. The judiciary is not closing its eyes to those people who were displaced. The judiciary is not looking at the names of a big man called Atiku Abubakar and David Mark.” On his assertion that Atiku’s absence from the 2027 presidential ballot would not cause any major consequence, Keyamo said he was speaking from the APC’s experience in Zamfara State, where a court ruling several years ago led to the removal of all the party’s elected candidates, including the governor, deputy governor, senators and members of the National and State Assemblies. He noted that the development did not cause the country to collapse, which informed his position on the possibility of Atiku being excluded from the 2027 race. He said, “Heaven did not fall when the same court sacked all our candidates in Zamfara a few years ago. Not just who were candidates who had won elections. Governor, the Deputy Governor, all members of the House of Assembly, all the Senators, and all the members of the House of Representatives. I’m talking from top to bottom. They were all sacked.” Keyamo said the APC accepted the decisions at the time and questioned why similar judicial outcomes involving opposition parties should now be portrayed as evidence of political interference. item.title: Ogun: INEC silent as court orders it to restore Adebutu’s name within 24hrs
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has yet to react officially to a Federal High Court judgment directing it to publish Oladipupo Adebutu’s name as the Peoples Democratic Party PDP candidate for the 2027 Ogun governorship election, saying it only read about the ruling on social media. The Director of Voter Education and Publicity at INEC, Mrs Victoria Messi-Eta, said she read about the judgment in the media and would get a response from the commission’s legal department. As of the time of filing this report, she had yet to revert. The National Commissioner in charge of Voter Education and Publicity, Malam Mohammed Haruna, neither returned calls nor responded to messages sent to him on the matter. The commission’s silence came after Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court in Abuja ordered INEC on Friday to publish Adebutu’s name within 24 hours. Delivering judgment, Justice Lifu held that INEC had no powers to unilaterally remove the name of a validly nominated candidate by a political party. He held that the commission’s action was unconstitutional, unlawful and of no effect. The judge said only the Federal High Court or the state high court had the power to declare a candidate invalid, not the commission. He also held that INEC breached Adebutu’s right to fair hearing, and dismissed the commission’s preliminary objection, declaring the suit competent. The PDP and Adebutu filed the suit on Oct. 22 after his name was removed from the list of contestants for the Ogun governorship seat. INEC was the sole defendant. Their lawyer, Ahmed Raji, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), sought 11 reliefs, including an order setting aside the commission’s decision to omit, remove or refuse to publish Adebutu’s name in the final list of candidates published on Oct. 10, for denial of fair hearing and violation of Sections 29 and 32 of the Electoral Act, 2026. They also asked the court to compel “the defendant to, within twenty-four (24) hours of the order/orders of this honourable court, include and/or publish the name of the 2nd plaintiff as the 1st plaintiff’s governorship candidate for Ogun State in the forthcoming 2027 General Election.” The post Ogun: INEC silent as court orders it to restore Adebutu’s name within 24hrs appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Burkina issues ‘terrorist’ warrants for journalists, activists
item.description: Burkinabe authorities said Friday they had issued arrest warrants for some 20 people, including journalists, activists, a former minister and former officers in exile over alleged “terrorism” offences. Ouagadougou Court of Appeal attorney general Desire Sawadogo said 14 arrest warrants with extradition requests had been issued, alongside seven further standard warrants. Burkina Faso, mired in jihadist violence for a decade, is governed by a junta that seized power in September 2022. It has cracked down hard on any criticism. Those targeted include Newton Ahmed Barry, a journalist for Radio France Internationale as well as former foreign minister Djibril Bassole, several officers and cyberactivists. They are accused of “complicity in forming a terrorist criminal organisation and complicity in the financing of terrorism”, as well as “forming a terrorist criminal organisation”, “glorifying terrorism” and “incitement to rebellion”. Also among those targeted, albeit not by a warrant, is the Ivorian influencer Camille Makosso, known for diatribes against Sahel region juntas and who has some four million social media followers. The justice ministry said Friday evening it was calling for legal proceedings in his country of residence” and hoped Ivory Coast would heed the request “in the name of international judicial cooperation.” Sawadogo said “media such as France 24” were also in the authorities’ sights. According to the prosecutor, more than six cases involving over 45 individuals and legal entities are currently under investigation by Burkina Faso’s specialised anti-terror judicial unit. The Public Prosecutor’s Office also stated that it had sought Meta’s cooperation to identify the administrators of pages of contributors accused of glorifying terrorism and to bring legal proceedings against the posts’ authors. item.title: 2027: Wike Criticises Obi Over National Anthem Snub At NDC Lagos Town Hall Meeting
item.description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has said that the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, demonstrated lawlessness and an intent to divide Nigeria by allegedly refusing to recite the official one. Wike made these remarks on Friday, during a stakeholders’ town hall meeting in Ogu-Bolo Local Government Area of Rivers State, organised under the banner of the Rainbow Coalition to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election bid and All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates. ﻿ Addressing traditional rulers, community leaders, youths, and party faithful, the FCT minister argued that a leader who disregards national symbols cannot be trusted with the presidency. “A whole national anthem of a country is being sung. A man who wants to be President of Nigeria would disobey and sit down. And then not only that, when a different national anthem that is not being used for Nigeria [was sung], he stood up. “In a way, he does not belong to this country. In a way, he has said he does not belong to this country; that if you give him the president, he would do a different thing that will divide Nigeria. “A man who does not believe in Nigeria, someone who derives joy in ridiculing the country by disrespecting its symbolic National Anthem must not be allowed to come near the presidency of our country,” the minister said. Wike further criticised Obi’s political trajectory and past governance record, alleging that the former Anambra State governor frequently abandons political parties whenever internal crises arise, rather than staying to resolve them. He also faulted Obi for not conducting local government elections during his eight-year tenure as governor, describing it as a contradiction to his professed belief in the rule of law. Tackles Atiku, Amaechi In addition to targeting Obi, the FCT Minister took aim at the opposition coalition involving former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi. Wike questioned their track records in public office, specifically citing the state of seaports during Amaechi’s tenure as Minister of Transportation and alleging that the administration demolished Government Secondary School, Ogu, without rebuilding it, alongside unfulfilled promises regarding a 1,000-bed specialist hospital. Urging the people of Ogu-Bolo to disregard what he termed “big grammar” from opposition politicians on television, Wike maintained that President Bola Tinubu’s administration had delivered tangible dividends of democracy to the area. He pointed to the construction of the Ogu-Bolo Civic Centre—facilitated through the federal appointment of an indigene, Boma Iyaye—as well as the conduct of local government elections. He urged people in the area to massively support the re-election of Tinubu, Kingsley Chinda for Governor of Rivers State and all the APC candidates seeking National Assembly seats. item.title: COREN Commends Nile university as 261 Engineering graduates take professional oath
item.description: Nile University of Nigeria has inducted 261 graduates of its Faculty of Engineering into the Nigerian Society of Engineers (NSE) and administered the Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria (COREN) oath in its maiden Induction and Oath-Taking Ceremony, as the institution intensifies efforts to align its programmes with international standards. The ceremony marks a significant milestone for the University’s Faculty of Engineering, which was established in 2009 and has grown into one of its flagship academic units, offering programmes in Civil Engineering, Computer Engineering, Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, and Petroleum and Gas Engineering. Prof. Prema A. Kirubakaran, who represented the Vice-Chancellor, described the ceremony as a landmark achievement for the Faculty and urged the newly inducted engineers to uphold the values of integrity, responsibility and continuous learning throughout their careers. Delivering the keynote address, Engr. Dr. Adamu Muhammed, MNSE, MNSChE, PMP, AMIChemE, Terminal Manager, NNPC Limited, praised Nile University of Nigeria for its contribution to engineering education, describing the institution as one capable of standing alongside leading universities globally. He challenged the new engineers to remain honest, continue learning and apply their knowledge to solving Nigeria’s developmental challenges. He urged the graduates to build careers defined by innovation, discipline and professional excellence. Speaking at the ceremony, Engr. Prof. Okorie Austine Uchegbusi Uche, FNSE, Registrar of COREN, commended Nile University of Nigeria for its implementation of Outcome-Based Education (OBE), describing it as one of the few institutions in the country actively applying the approach, which emphasises measurable competencies and graduate outcomes. Reflecting on the significance of the occasion, the Dean of the Faculty of Engineering, Engr. Prof. Abdulhameed Danjuma Mambo, said the induction signified the graduates’ readiness to assume the responsibilities of professional engineering practice. “Graduation shows that you have learned, but induction shows that you have become a professional,” he said. According to him, while members of the public may never see the calculations behind engineering projects, they place their trust in the professionalism and judgment of engineers responsible for them. Prof. Mambo said the Faculty remains committed to producing graduates equipped with the technical knowledge, professional values and practical skills required to contribute to national development. He noted that the ongoing accreditation activities involving the Faculty form part of efforts to ensure that its programmes meet global standards and remain competitive internationally.
